summary: scripts/st-test --push tops up a green run that main overtook: it merges the base in when the gate would judge the merge, signs only what the new tree lacks (every check after any merge, also for a narrowed run), and pushes the branch the moment it is covered; after 3 rounds it fails with 'main is moving too fast; run again'. Before any wait it checks for nix (PATH, then the system and profile locations) and, with --push, for a git identity; a --base commit ID reads its repository through origin

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The run record gains top_up (the round number); a top-up round is not a full run.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes. What a note covers and how the gate judges it are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Runs re-execute main's st-test, so this applies to every run once on main. A green whole-suite --push run now pushes its branch itself; the caller's own git push afterwards has nothing left to send.

manual.detail: None. A run started from a systemd-run --user unit should pass --setenv=PATH="$PATH"; without nix it now fails at once instead of after the wait.
